reason: This is the only available action, and it starts the muscle-cell lineage needed for the goal.
expectation: I expect the progenitors to become muscle precursors, though the precise stage is uncertain.

effect: The progenitors became aligned myoblasts, ready for the fusion step.
reaction: The single nuclei and alignment make the next construction clear.
reason: Fusion is the only offered combination and should build the muscle fibre needed for the goal.
expectation: I expect the myoblasts to fuse into a shared, multinucleated muscle fibre.

effect: Fusion produced multinucleated fibres with space for the pulling machinery.
reaction: The retained nuclei make the fusion result easy to follow.
reason: The only offered combination adds the filament machinery needed for a pull.
expectation: I expect the fibre to gain organized actin and myosin, though it may need a calcium signal before it can pull.

effect: The fibre now contains actin and myosin, but the grip sites remain covered, so it is not yet pulling.
reaction: The reset myosin inset clarifies the starting state, though how calcium exposes the sites remains to be shown.
reason: The only offered combination supplies the calcium signal needed to initiate a pull.
expectation: I expect calcium to expose actin's grip sites so myosin can attach and pull.

effect: Calcium exposed the grip sites, allowing ATP-dependent myosin cycling and filament sliding; the fibre now needs to reset.
reaction: The contrast between shortening fibre and unchanged filament lengths is useful.
reason: The only offered combination should remove calcium and prepare the fibre to pull again.
expectation: I expect ATP-powered pumps to return calcium to storage, allowing the grip sites to be covered again.

effect: ATP-powered calcium pumping stopped the pull and reset the fibre; the next goal is to build and attach both muscles.
reaction: It's useful that relaxation requires ATP and that an outside pull lengthens the fibre.
reason: The only offered combination adds extracellular matrix, apparently beginning the muscle construction.
expectation: I expect the matrix to support or bundle the fibres into muscle tissue, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The matrix organized fibres into fascicles, with enough bundles for both muscles.
reaction: The distinction between the fibre membrane and surrounding connective layer makes the structure clearer.
reason: I'll build the biceps first using its sheaths and tendons; both muscles are needed.
expectation: I expect the fascicles to fill the biceps sheaths and form a muscle with tendon routes ready for attachment.

alternatives.reason: The triceps also needs building; I chose the biceps first without a strong reason to prefer the order.

effect: The biceps now has two filled heads and tendons ready for attachment; fascicles remain available for the triceps.
reaction: The force pathway from fibres through connective tissue to tendon is a useful detail.
reason: I'll build the triceps before attaching the two muscles to the skeleton.
expectation: I expect fascicles to fill the triceps sheaths, forming a muscle with tendons ready for attachment.

alternatives.reason: Attaching the biceps now would also advance the goal, but I prefer to build both muscles first.

effect: Both muscles are built; their tendons still need attachment to the skeleton.
reaction: The three triceps heads and common tendon distinguish it from the biceps, though the force inset repeats.
reason: I'll attach the biceps first to advance the goal; either muscle could come first.
expectation: I expect its tendons to connect the biceps across the elbow, enabling a bending pull.

alternatives.reason: The triceps also needs attachment, but I chose to start with the biceps.

effect: The biceps is attached and shown flexing the elbow; the assembly still needs an extensor.
reaction: The two poses make the biceps tendon’s bending action clear.
reason: The only offered combination attaches the triceps to fill the extensor slot.
expectation: I expect the triceps to attach across the elbow and provide a pull that straightens it.

effect: The triceps completed the assembly, showing how its posterior attachment produces elbow extension while the biceps flexes it. Both goals are complete.
reaction: The contrasting attachment positions make the opposite movements clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: The calcium-triggered contraction was most worthwhile: the planned sequence connects ATP-dependent myosin cycling to a shortening fibre while showing that the filaments themselves do not shorten.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the triceps repeated the biceps force-pathway inset; the different heads and tendon were useful, but that part felt repetitive.

surprise.text: Relaxation uses ATP to pump calcium back into storage, and the fibre lengthens under an outside pull rather than actively pushing itself longer.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the biceps-first order was arbitrary. The lineage picture also uses 'paraxial' without explaining it, making that connection less accessible than the later constructions.

continue.text: I would continue: connecting the same pulling machinery to opposite elbow movements makes me curious about how subsequent systems fit together. The early sequence was fairly linear, though.
